paragraphs.source_en: Following Hideyoshi's instructions, Ieyasu had Maeda Gen'i arrange a banquet in the great hall of Osaka Castle. The seating arrangement was entirely different from the previous day's. Hideyoshi's chair was raised high in the center; Ieyasu and seven others sat in chairs to either side, while the two Ming envoys knelt before Hideyoshi. That day Hideyoshi again attended wearing the ceremonial crown bestowed by the Great Ming and a scarlet Chinese robe; the seven senior retainers were likewise most imposing. The state letter was presented to Hideyoshi, who ordered that the monk Jōtai be summoned to read it aloud.
